expectations.text: Explains config-as-data model in plain language
expectations.evidence: 'ConfigHub treats configuration as data, not templates. Fully materialized YAML lives in a versioned database; you mutate it through server-side functions.'

expectations.text: Names all primary entities (Space, Unit, Revision, Function, Trigger, Filter, Link, Target, Worker, ApplyGate)
expectations.evidence: Each entity has its own bullet with a one-line description; ApplyGate covered alongside Trigger

expectations.text: Uses current terminology (Revision / --change-desc / --display-mutation / Evidence / review links)
expectations.evidence: Uses Revision, --change-desc, --display-mutation consistently; no 'receipts' or 'trust surface'

expectations.text: Grounds in live state by running read-only queries
expectations.evidence: 'you already have four [Spaces]: default, test-space, platform, skill-examples' and 'hello-app (the workload)'

expectations.text: Routes to specific skills per user intent
expectations.evidence: Provided a routing list mapping each intent (install worker, apply, mutate, query, policy, verify, completion) to a named skill
Only cub space list / unit list were executed
'cub unit get hello-app --space skill-examples --web will open it'
